summary: Find the longest contiguous palindromic substring of s.
mainInsight: Every palindrome has a centre (a character or a gap between two). Expand outwards from each of the 2n - 1 centres while the two ends match and keep the longest span. This is O(n^2) time with O(1) space; Manacher's algorithm does it in O(n).

approaches.summary: Check every substring for being a palindrome.

approaches.name: Expand around centre
approaches.summary: For each index expand for odd and even length palindromes.

approaches.name: 2D DP
approaches.summary: dp[i][j] is true if s[i..j] is a palindrome: s[i] == s[j] and dp[i+1][j-1].

approaches.name: Manacher
approaches.summary: Reuse palindrome radii mirrored around the rightmost centre.
weaknesses: Hard to derive in an interview

commonMistakes: Returning the length instead of the substring
Off-by-one when slicing after the expansion overshoots by one on each side
edgeCases: No repeated characters (answer is any single character)

promptVariants: Why must you try both odd and even centres?
What goes wrong if only single-character centres are expanded?
cards.answer: Palindromes of even length (e.g. 'abba') have no single middle character; their centre is the gap between two equal letters. Expanding only from single characters would miss every even-length palindrome, so each index i is expanded as (i, i) and (i, i + 1).
keyPoints: Even palindromes centre on a gap

cards.explanation: n centres, each expansion can take O(n).

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def longestPalindrome(self, s: str) -> str:
        best_l, best_r = 0, 0

        def expand(l: int, r: int) -> None:
            nonlocal best_l, best_r
            while l >= 0 and r < len(s) and s[l] == s[r]:   # grow while the ends match
                l -= 1
                r += 1
            if (r - 1) - (l + 1) > best_r - best_l:          # span of the last valid palindrome
                best_l, best_r = l + 1, r - 1

        for i in range(len(s)):
            expand(i, i)        # odd-length centre
            expand(i, i + 1)    # even-length centre
        return s[best_l:best_r + 1]
